_cdcBulk: §10gp, the bulk CDC apply. Which events of one batch may share ONE upsert (cdcBulkSql: chainBulkSql with NO version guard — two updates of a row in one PostgreSQL transaction carry the same version; the stream's order is the truth and SQLite applies json_each's rows in order, the last occurrence of a key winning: measured on 3.53.4) and which take the per-event path, named. `tables[t].columns` is the replica table's OWN column list (the reverted probe experiment judged a whole payload against the descriptor and lost 28 of 60 batches). A `bulk` segment's `events` are the batch indexes it stands for: the shell still feeds the HLC floor, confirms echoes and notifies per event, and on a failed statement applies those events one at a time. Tables interleave (one transaction, FK checks deferred); within a table the order is the stream's, so a per-event event of the same table closes its run first. The rows keep the wire's JSON shapes; json_extract binds them as chainRowParams does. How a shell EXECUTES a bulk segment is its own measured choice: zb-client-ts binds one prepared per-row upsert per row (faster than the json_each statement on better-sqlite3, NOTES §10hd) and commits up to 20,000 events per transaction; the json_each text stays pinned as `sql`. DuckDB is bulk-capable too (§10hg): libzb executes a segment through the appender into a temp table and ONE set-based upsert, keys de-duplicated to their last occurrence first — row-at-a-time upserts exhaust DuckDB's memory; the `sql` text is SQLite's and a DuckDB shell ignores it.
